text:
maya: heads up — we just saw a weird duplicate event delivery on SSE reconnects for a single-tenant customer. repro steps and logs below.

alex: ugh, details?

maya: client opens SSE -> receives events A,B -> connection stalls (no FIN) for ~45s at edge proxy -> client reconnects with Last-Event-ID=A -> server replays starting from A -> client gets A again (duplicate).

sam: is the server actually re-sending A or is the proxy replaying buffered bytes?

maya: looks like proxy. tcpdump from edge shows the original stream still in kernel send buffer when client reconnects. proxy then flushes leftover bytes to new socket.

olivia: so it's a buffering/half-close detection issue at the proxy, not our resume logic?

maya: yes. resume flow on our side treats reconnect as idempotent and will re-emit if requested, but we rely on upstream socket lifecycle to be closed. here the proxy keeps the old connection half-open and then forwards buffered chunks to the new connection.

infra-bot: Deploy job #deploy-1723 completed on edge-proxy pool-3 at 2026-03-20T09:10:12Z :white_check_mark:

alex: what proxy version and settings? anyone changed keepalive or tcp_delack?

maya: proxy v2.7.1, default keepalive 60s, proxy sets SO_LINGER off. A couple of recent kernel patches changed write coalescing on our image in last rollout (kernel 5.15.x -> 5.15.y).

sam: hmm. If keepalive is long, and proxy doesn't detect client half-close quickly, buffered data could stick around. We should consider TCP_USER_TIMEOUT or turning on TCP_NODELAY for SSE streams.

olivia: node apps open streams too; will TCP_NODELAY cause perf regressions for small events?

alex: for SSE we usually send small text frames. Disabling Nagle (NODELAY) reduces small-packet latency but increases packets. tradeoff might be ok for streams with SLO.

maya: telemetry gap: console shows a reconnect event and server-side resume, but we don't mark "stalled at proxy" — packet-level buffering not visible in existing metrics. ops alerted but dashboards don't show proxy-queued-bytes.

sam: can we emit a marker when we observe resumed bytes with id <= last-sent? i.e., detect duplicate replay and tag it to a new metric?

alex: it's tricky because if client legitimately asks for overlap (Last-Event-ID is inclusive) we can't tell whether duplicates came from proxy or server. we need proxy metrics.

olivia: short-term mitigations?

maya: options proposed:
- Reduce proxy keepalive to 15s (edge config)
- Enable TCP_USER_TIMEOUT on proxy sockets so stale connections fail faster
- Add a proxy metric: per-conn queued_bytes and expose in console sample dashboards
- Server-side: idempotent dedupe on event IDs for N seconds as last-resort\n
alex: prefer proxy-side fixes first. We should avoid server dedupe because some clients expect inclusive replay.

sam: ping @infra-team — do we have ability to toggle keepalive globally for that pool?

olivia: @infra-team FYI: request to try keepalive=15s on pool-3 for 1h canary. Also want queued_bytes gauge.

infra-bot: @infra-team alert: config change request — keepalive=15s on pool-3. Approvers: ops-leads.

maya: I ran a small sim locally with socat and a proxy stub. Repro script:
```
# server: stream 1..5 with small sleeps
while true; do for i in 1 2 3 4 5; do echo "data: $i\n\n"; sleep 1; done; done
# proxy: accept, forward, then simulate stall by pausing drain for 45s
```
Result: when client reconnects immediately, proxy forwards buffered chunk 1 again.

alex: good repro. can we add a quick health check to console showing "stalled-by-proxy" if queued_bytes > threshold for > X seconds?

olivia: yes, but need proxy to export queued_bytes. we can add a lightweight sfx counter and a prometheus gauge on the proxy side. low-risk.

sam: for rollout UX: console should surface "possible duplicate events" on reconnects when proxy-stage metrics indicate buffered-forwarding. That helps support triage.

maya: agree. Also add a note in the resume docs about edge buffering behavior and how Last-Event-ID inclusive semantics can produce duplicates if proxies buffer.

alex: decision items:
1) infra to canary keepalive=15s on pool-3 for 2 hours — if no regressions, extend.
2) proxy: add queued_bytes gauge + export to prometheus (low risk).
3) console: add a dashboard tile and an alert when queued_bytes per-conn > 32KB for >30s.
4) product docs: add guidance about duplicate events and dedupe responsibilities.

olivia: I'll own console tile and alert. maya will own repro and docs. infra to own canary. sam will scope proxy metric change. alex to coordinate release.

maya: timeline? infra canary today afternoon PST?

infra-bot: @infra-team scheduled canary: pool-3 keepalive change at 2026-03-20T16:00:00Z. Rollback window 2 hours.

sam: I'll open a tiny PR to proxy repo with queued_bytes export and a config toggle for NODELAY/TCP_USER_TIMEOUT. link: https://git.rex/proxy/changes/485

alex: thanks. after canary we should run the customer repro against the canary endpoints and confirm duplicates stop.

maya: will coordinate and post results in thread. thanks everyone :thumbsup:

olivia: thanks — also file a support blurb to notify the affected tenant about expected brief canary windows.

maya: filing now.
